subject: Computer Networking
title: Quantum Networking Basics
description: Learn Quantum Networking Basics in one minute.

hook.text: Quantum physics builds communication channels impossible to eavesdrop on. Real technology, not theory.

buildup.text: QKD sends encryption keys encoded in photons. Measuring a photon changes it irreversibly.

discovery.text: Intercepting a photon changes it detectably. Both sides know the key was compromised.

twist.text: Quantum networks can't carry regular data — too fragile. They distribute keys for conventional use.

climax.text: China's QUESS satellite showed QKD over 1,200 km. It works but scaling is the hard part.

punchline.text: Quantum makes eavesdropping impossible. Security from physics itself.

quiz.question: Why can't quantum key distribution be eavesdropped on?
options: Measuring a quantum photon changes it, revealing the interception
The keys are too complex for any computer to decode
Quantum data travels faster than light

details.summary: Quantum networking uses quantum mechanical properties like entanglement and superposition to transmit information in ways impossible with classical networks. Quantum key distribution creates provably secure encryption keys. Entanglement-based networks could enable unhackable communication channels.
details.whyItMatters: Quantum networking promises communication security based on the laws of physics rather than computational difficulty. It addresses the long-term threat of quantum computers breaking current encryption.
takeaways: Quantum key distribution creates theoretically unbreakable encryption
Entangled particles enable secure communication over distance
Any eavesdropping attempt detectably disturbs quantum states

faq.question: How does quantum key distribution work?
faq.answer: QKD sends encryption keys encoded in quantum states of photons. The laws of quantum mechanics guarantee that any interception attempt disturbs the photon states detectably. If eavesdropping is detected, the key is discarded.

faq.question: When will quantum networks be practical?
faq.answer: Point-to-point QKD links are commercially available today over distances up to about 100 kilometers. China operates a 2,000-kilometer QKD backbone. However, a full quantum internet with quantum repeaters and long-distance entanglement distribution is likely a decade or more away.
